answer: Require each trading identity to lock a separate, refundable $100 bond until 30 days after it exits. The admission signal is an escrow receipt bound to one key, so aliases named whisper and dune cannot share a deposit. Every extra fake identity needs another $100 locked. At a 12% annual capital cost, an alias active for one day costs about $1.02 over its 31-day lock, even if it behaves perfectly. This makes mass registration costly without proving who owns a key.
